subject: How to rename data-set tags such that previous results are still found

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: How to rename data-set tags such that previous results are still found
parts:
Hi,

with aroma.affymetrix v0.8.2 a few updates where made in how and what
tags are appended to output data sets. These updates will in some
cases cause aroma.affymetrix not to find previously process data,
because it looks for directory names where the tags are in a different
order. The solution is simply to rename all coinsurances to meet
these newer tags.

Here are a few cases where I can see you have to manually rename
directories. You might experience other cases. Basically, if you
find that your running the same script but aroma.affymetrix is not
finding the results, use verbose output and look where
aroma.affymetrix is searching now and rename your old results
accordingly. Here are some examples showing you how to avoid
reprocessing:

1) COPY-NUMBER ANALYSIS:
If you previously did something like:

plm <- AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE,
tags=c("+300", "*"))
plm$shift <- +300;

the output data set would be something like:

plmData/Foo_2007,ACC,-XY,+300,AVG/

Two things, now you should just do:

plm <- AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE shift=+300)

and the output data set would become:

plmData/Foo_2007,ACC,-XY,AVG,+300/

Note the reordering of the last two tags. Thus, if you want to the
new code to detect you previously processed results, you should rename
all directories by swapping tags '+300,AVG' to 'AVG,+300' in all
occurrences in plmData/, gladData/, cbsData/, and reports/. If not,
aroma.affymetrix will just reprocess you data.


2) EXON ANALYSIS:
If you previously did something like:

plm <- ExonRmaPlm(cs, mergeGroups=TRUE, tags=c("*", "main"))

the output data set would previously be something like:

plmData/Foo_2007,RBC,QN,RMA,main,merged/

whereas in the new version the 'merged' tag comes after RMA, i.e.

plmData/Foo_2007,RBC,QN,RMA,merged,main/

This only applies if you explicitly added an extra tag as above, but
otherwise not. For the same reason as above, you should then go
through all directories an rename the dataset directories from having
tags 'RMA,main,merged' to 'RMA,merged,main'.


3a) FIRMA ANALYSIS:
Previously FIRMA estimates would output data to root directory
modelFirmaModel/. Now its output ends up in firmaData/. Just rename
root directory modelFirmaModel/ to firmaData/.

3b) FIRMA ANALYSIS:
Previously the FIRMA model would drop tags from the input data set (a
mistake), e.g. the output would be

modelFirmaModel/Foo_2007,FIRMA/

whereas now it is something like:

firmaData/Foo_2007,RBC,QN,RMA,merged,FIRMA/

You should rename your old FIRMA data sets so that the have the proper tags.

Finally, note that some results cached to file (in ~/.Rcache/) will be
reprocessed. There is no workaround for this, but they are on the
other hand "one timers".

Hope this helps

/Henrik
